subject: biology
title: Organisation Adventure
welcome_lead: From a single cell up to a whole organism — meet the levels of life.
meta_desc: GCSE Biology Organisation walkthrough — cell to tissue to organ to organ system, plus human and plant tissue examples.
final_note: You learned the levels of organisation, named four human tissues (epithelial, muscle, glandular, connective), and four plant tissues (epidermal, mesophyll, xylem, phloem).

concepts.def: Group of similar cells doing the same job
Group of tissues working together (e.g. stomach)
Lines and covers surfaces of the body
Plant tissue — carries water and minerals up
Plant tissue — carries dissolved sugars around

walkthroughs.body_html:
Cell → Tissue → Organ → Organ system → Organism

- A cell is the basic unit.
- A tissue is many similar cells doing the same job.
- An organ is several tissues working together.
- An organ system is several organs working together.
- The whole organism is all the systems combined.

Four to know:

- Epithelial — lines surfaces (gut, lungs, skin).
- Muscle — contracts to make movement.
- Glandular — makes and releases secretions like enzymes or hormones.
- Connective — holds things together (bone, cartilage, blood).

The stomach is a great example — it has all four.

Plants are organised too. A leaf is an organ. Inside it:

- Epidermal tissue — covers the leaf (with a waxy cuticle).
- Palisade mesophyll — packed with chloroplasts for photosynthesis.
- Xylem — carries water up from the roots.
- Phloem — carries dissolved sugars around the plant.

mcqs.q: Which is the correct order of organisation?
options: Organ → tissue → cell
Cell → tissue → organ → organ system
Tissue → cell → organ → system

mcqs.q: Which plant tissue transports water up from the roots?
options: Phloem
Xylem
Mesophyll
Epidermis

mcqs.q: What drives water up the xylem in a tall tree?
options: Competition means physically fighting and is rare in nature.
Roots actively pump water up to the leaves like a heart.
Transpiration pull — evaporation from leaves creates tension that pulls water up the continuous water column.
Capillary action alone is enough to lift water to the top of any tree.

mcqs.q: In osmosis, which direction does water move?
options: From a region of higher water potential (less concentrated solution) to lower water potential.
Water moves from high solute concentration to low solute concentration.
Capillary action alone is enough to lift water to the top of any tree.
Water moves towards the sugar because sugar attracts water molecules chemically.

mcqs.q: Why is interspecific competition between similar species important?
options: Competition means physically fighting and is rare in nature.
Water moves towards the sugar because sugar attracts water molecules chemically.
Two species cannot occupy exactly the same niche indefinitely — competition often leads to displacement or niche divergence.
Competition only happens between predators and their prey.

mcqs.q: A stomach contains epithelial, muscle, glandular and connective tissue. How many DIFFERENT tissue types is that?
The stomach is made of muscle, glandular and epithelial tissues working together to digest food. The stomach is therefore best described as a(n):
options: Organ
Tissue
Organ system
Cell

mcqs.q: Which sequence shows the levels of organisation from smallest to largest?
options: Cell → tissue → organ → organ system → organism
Organism → organ → tissue → cell
Tissue → cell → organ → organism
Organ → cell → tissue → organism

mcqs.q: Xylem and phloem are grouped together because they both:
options: Form transport tissue in plants
Carry out photosynthesis
Store starch in the root
Control gas exchange at the leaf

mcqs.q: Epithelial tissue lines the inside of the gut. Which best describes the role of a tissue?
options: A group of similar cells carrying out the same function
A single cell with one job
A group of different organs
The whole organ system
